item.title: 🔵 Java Spring Boot "heapdump" scans, (Mon, Jul 27th)
item.description:
Why this matters: Hospitality system impact — check guest-facing services and PMS/POS status.

Spring Boot exposes the endpoint "/actuator/heapdump" to collect debug information. By default, the endpoint will return a file heapdump.hprof, which includes a binary heapdump that can be used to analyze the current state of the application. Non-Java readers may be familiar with a similar concept, core dumps, which are produced by binaries to expose a memory image at the time the software crashes. "heapdumps" are the Java analog to "core-dumps". The heapdump often includes secrets used by the application to connect to backend systems. API keys, database passwords, and other sensitive data may be exposed in the heapdump.



Source: SANS Internet Storm Center  |  Severity: FYI  |  Age: 7h ago

item.title: 🟠 A Record-Breaking Patch Tuesday for June 2026
item.description:
Why this matters: Leadership context — useful for risk, budget, and vendor conversations.
Microsoft today released software updates to plug nearly 200 security holes across its Windows operating systems and supported software, a record number of fixes for the company's monthly Patch Tuesday cycle. Nearly three dozen of those bugs earned Microsoft's most dire "critical" rating, and exploit code for at least three of the weaknesses is now publicly available.

Source: Krebs on Security  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 47d ago

item.title: 🔵 Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
item.description:
Why this matters: RCE vulnerability — patch immediately, check for exposed attack surface.
The Instagram accounts for the Obama White House and the Chief Master Sergeant of the U.S. Space Force were briefly defaced with pro-Iranian images and messages over the weekend, after instructions began circulating on Telegram showing how to trick Meta's "AI support assistant" bot into resetting account passwords.

Source: Krebs on Security  |  Severity: FYI  |  Age: 56d ago
